Arithmetic with an explicit overflow policy

Source: R/ops.R
zuint-arith.Rd

The operators +, -, *, %/%, %%, ^ and unary minus give NA with one warning of class zuint_overflow_warning per call when a result is out of range. These functions choose differently:

Usage

checked_add(x, y)

checked_sub(x, y)

checked_mul(x, y)

checked_idiv(x, y)

checked_mod(x, y)

checked_pow(x, y)

checked_neg(x)

wrapping_add(x, y)

wrapping_sub(x, y)

wrapping_mul(x, y)

wrapping_pow(x, y)

wrapping_neg(x)

Arguments

x, y

zuint vectors, or a zuint vector and a logical, integer or double vector. They are recycled.

Value

A zuint vector of the common type.

Details

  • checked_*() raise an error of class zuint_overflow_error instead.

  • wrapping_*() compute modulo \(2^{64}\) or \(2^{128}\), for hashing and checksums. A result that wraps onto the type's NA bit pattern is NA: NA-ness never depends on the policy. A negative integer operand of an unsigned type wraps too.

Operands take their common type first (see zu_common_type()). %/% rounds towards negative infinity and %% takes the sign of the divisor, as in R; division by zero is NA, except in checked_idiv() and checked_mod(), where it is an error of class zuint_division_error. / divides in double. ^ is exact for a non-negative integer exponent and computed in double otherwise. Comparison is exact across all the types and doubles.

Examples

x <- int64("9223372036854775807")
x + 1L
#> Warning: 1 result is out of range. NA produced.
#> <int64[1]>
#> [1] NA
try(checked_add(x, 1L))
#> Error in checked_add(x, 1L) : 1 result is out of range.
wrapping_add(x, 2L)
#> <int64[1]>
#> [1] -9223372036854775807
wrapping_mul(uint64("18446744073709551614"), 31L)
#> <uint64[1]>
#> [1] 18446744073709551554
checked_pow(int128(2), 126L)
#> <int128[1]>
#> [1] 85070591730234615865843651857942052864
